questionsAcceptableUse.question: An employee wants to use their USC email and cloud storage to help run a small side business they own, only during their unpaid lunch break. Is this acceptable under the policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, as long as it's limited to unpaid break time.

options.label: B
options.text: No — personal use must not be associated with any for-profit outside business activity, regardless of timing.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, if their manager gives verbal approval.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, as long as it's under 30 minutes per day.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 3.1 states personal use must not be associated with any for-profit outside business activity. The fact that the activity occurs during unpaid break time does not change that restriction.

questionsAcceptableUse.question: A colleague is locked out of their own account and asks to use your login just this once to finish an urgent task. What should you do?

options.label: A
options.text: Share your credentials since it's a one-time favour for a colleague.

options.label: B
options.text: Share your credentials, then change your password afterward.

options.label: C
options.text: Decline — employees must use only their own log-on ID and password, and credentials must not be shared.

options.label: D
options.text: Share your credentials only if you stay logged in to supervise.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 4.2 requires personnel to use their own log-on ID and password only, and prohibits sharing credentials.

questionsAcceptableUse.question: Your work laptop has been running slowly, and you suspect the antivirus software is the cause. What does the policy require?

options.label: A
options.text: You may disable it temporarily and re-enable it the same day.

options.label: B
options.text: You must not disable antivirus software; report the issue instead.

options.label: C
options.text: You may disable it outside of business hours.

options.label: D
options.text: You may disable it if you notify a coworker first.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 4.1 states users must not disable antivirus software and should report virus occurrences or related issues.

questionsAcceptableUse.question: After a frustrating call with a vendor, an employee sends a profanity-laced, angry email about them using the corporate email system. Which part of the policy does this violate?

options.label: A
options.text: Section 3, Personal Use.

options.label: B
options.text: Section 2, Corporate Public Image, which prohibits abusive or profane communications through corporate systems.

options.label: C
options.text: Section 6, Data Protection.

options.label: D
options.text: Section 7, Working From Home.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 2.1 prohibits abusive, discriminatory, harassing, inflammatory, profane, or offensive communications on corporate systems.

questionsAcceptableUse.question: An employee is working from home on their personal laptop and needs to store USC member files locally to complete a project. What must be true of that laptop under the policy?

options.label: A
options.text: Nothing additional is required, since it is the employee's own device.

options.label: B
options.text: It must be patched to the latest secure version, run up-to-date security software, and be password protected.

options.label: C
options.text: The files must be printed rather than stored digitally.

options.label: D
options.text: It only needs COO approval to be used this way.

questionsAcceptableUse.explanation: Section 7.1 requires personal devices accessing USC data to be patched, running current security software, and password protected.

questionsCustomerService.question: A customer with a disability wants to bring their service animal into a USC public-facing space. What is the USC's approach?

options.label: A
options.text: Service animals are never permitted indoors.

options.label: B
options.text: The USC welcomes service animals onto premises open to the public, and commits to finding alternatives where animals are legally prohibited.

options.label: C
options.text: Only guide dogs are permitted; no other service animals.

options.label: D
options.text: A written doctor's note is required at every visit.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.2.1 states the USC welcomes persons with disabilities accompanied by a service animal onto premises open to the public, and commits to finding alternatives if service animals are prohibited by law.

questionsCustomerService.question: The USC needs to temporarily close an accessible entrance for repairs. What must it do?

options.label: A
options.text: Wait until the repair is finished before announcing anything.

options.label: B
options.text: Nothing, as long as repairs are completed quickly.

options.label: C
options.text: Notify customers promptly with a clearly posted notice including the reason, anticipated length, and available alternatives.

options.label: D
options.text: Only inform USC staff, not the public.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.4.1 requires prompt notification of service disruptions via a clearly posted notice including the reason, anticipated length, and alternatives, if available.

questionsCustomerService.question: A support person accompanies a customer with a disability into a paid event. If a fee applies to the support person, what must the USC do?

options.label: A
options.text: Charge the support person double the standard fee.

options.label: B
options.text: It is never permitted to charge a fee for a support person.

options.label: C
options.text: Always waive the fee automatically.

options.label: D
options.text: Communicate and post the fee accordingly through the USC's website, brochure, or other public methods.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.3.2 states that where a fee applies to a support person's admission, it will be communicated and posted through the USC's website, brochure, or other public methods.

questionsCustomerService.question: When must training on this policy be provided to a new employee who deals with the public?

options.label: A
options.text: As soon as practicable after being assigned applicable duties.

options.label: B
options.text: Within their first year, at any point.

options.label: C
options.text: Only during annual refresher sessions.

options.label: D
options.text: Only if the employee requests it.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.5.3 states training will be provided to each person as soon as practicable after being assigned applicable duties.

questionsCustomerService.question: A customer wants to provide feedback about their accessibility experience with the USC. How can this be submitted?

options.label: A
options.text: Only by mail.

options.label: B
options.text: In person, by telephone, in writing, or electronically via email or other digital formats.

options.label: C
options.text: Only through a third-party ombudsperson.

options.label: D
options.text: Feedback is not accepted from the general public.

questionsCustomerService.explanation: Section 4.6.1 states feedback can be given in person, by telephone, in writing, or electronically via email or other digital formats.

questionsAccessibility.question: An applicant is selected to participate in an interview process. What must the USC do regarding accommodations?

options.label: A
options.text: Accommodations are only discussed after the applicant's first 90 days of employment.

options.label: B
options.text: Nothing, unless the applicant is ultimately hired.

options.label: C
options.text: Notify the applicant that accommodations are available upon request, and consult with them to provide or arrange suitable accommodation.

options.label: D
options.text: Only offer accommodations after a formal complaint is filed.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.11.1 states the USC notifies job applicants selected for an assessment or selection process that accommodations are available upon request, and consults with and provides or arranges suitable accommodation.

questionsAccessibility.question: A customer's service animal isn't easily identifiable by a harness or vest, and staff need to confirm it's required for a disability. What can staff request?

options.label: A
options.text: A government-issued identification card for the animal.

options.label: B
options.text: Proof of veterinary vaccination only.

options.label: C
options.text: Nothing — staff may never ask for confirmation.

options.label: D
options.text: Documentation from a regulated health professional confirming the person needs the service animal for reasons relating to their disability.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.4.2 states staff may ask for documentation from a regulated health professional when a service animal cannot be easily identified.

questionsAccessibility.question: The USC is redesigning a service counter in a public space. What minimum clear knee space must it provide from the public-facing side, per this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: 750 mm wide x 680 mm high x 250 mm deep, with additional toe space beyond.

options.label: B
options.text: 1000 mm wide x 800 mm high x 300 mm deep.

options.label: C
options.text: No specific dimensions are required.

options.label: D
options.text: 500 mm wide x 500 mm high x 200 mm deep.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.12.3.1.a specifies clear knee space of 750 mm wide x 680 mm high x 250 mm deep below the service counter, with additional toe space of 750 mm wide x 230 mm high x 230 mm deep.

questionsAccessibility.question: An employee with a disability needs individualized workplace emergency information. When will the USC review this information?

options.label: A
options.text: Only once, when the employee is first hired.

options.label: B
options.text: When the employee changes location, when their accommodation needs or plans are reviewed, or when the employer reviews its general emergency response policies.

options.label: C
options.text: Only if requested in writing on an annual basis.

options.label: D
options.text: Never — this is handled entirely by the employee.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.11.7 lists these three triggers for reviewing individualized workplace emergency response information.

questionsAccessibility.question: A person with a disability requests an accessible format of a USC document. What cost, if any, can be charged?

options.label: A
options.text: A cost determined case-by-case with no cap.

options.label: B
options.text: A standard administrative fee.

options.label: C
options.text: No additional cost — the format will be provided at no additional cost and in a timely manner.

options.label: D
options.text: A cost equal to printing and shipping expenses.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.8.2 states the USC will provide accessible formats or communication supports at no additional cost and in a timely manner.

questionsAccessibility.question: If an assistive device presents a significant and unavoidable health or safety concern, what does the USC commit to doing?

options.label: A
options.text: Requiring a liability waiver with no further accommodation.

options.label: B
options.text: Charging an additional insurance fee.

options.label: C
options.text: Prohibiting the person with a disability from accessing the premises.

options.label: D
options.text: Using other measures to ensure the person with a disability can still access goods, services, or facilities.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.2.2 states that where an assistive device presents a significant and unavoidable health or safety concern, other measures will be used to ensure access.

questionsAccessibility.question: Before requiring a support person for health or safety reasons, what must the USC do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Consult with the person with a disability, consider available evidence, and determine there is no other reasonable way to protect health or safety.

options.label: B
options.text: Only obtain approval from the Senior Manager, Communications.

options.label: C
options.text: Post a general public notice, with no individual consultation required.

options.label: D
options.text: Nothing — it can require a support person unilaterally.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.5.5 requires consultation with the person with a disability, consideration of available evidence, and confirmation that no other reasonable option exists before making this decision.

questionsAccessibility.question: What accessibility standard must USC websites meet under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: WCAG 1.0 Level A.

options.label: B
options.text: WCAG 2.0 Level AA.

options.label: C
options.text: WCAG 2.1 Level AAA.

options.label: D
options.text: No specific standard is required.

questionsAccessibility.explanation: Section 5.10.5 states the USC will meet internationally-recognized WCAG 2.0 Level AA website requirements.

questionsConflict.question: An employee paid through honoraria wants to take on a second, separate paid USC staff role at the same time. Is this permitted?

options.label: A
options.text: No — paid employees, including those paid through honoraria, may hold only one USC position at a time.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, with only verbal manager approval.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, as long as combined hours stay under 40 per week.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, as long as the two roles don't overlap in duties.

questionsConflict.explanation: Section 5.1 states paid employees, including those paid through honoraria, shall hold one position with the USC at a time.

questionsConflict.question: A paid staff member wants to run for USC Councillor while continuing in their current paid role. What does the policy say?

options.label: A
options.text: It's permitted since Councillor is an elected, not paid, position.

options.label: B
options.text: Paid employees may not apply or run for Councillor while holding their paid position.

options.label: C
options.text: It's permitted only with Board of Directors approval.

options.label: D
options.text: It's permitted after six months in the paid role.

questionsConflict.explanation: Section 5.3 prohibits certain paid staff from applying or running for USC Councillor (and other listed positions) while they hold their paid position.

questionsConflict.question: A paid employee applies for a hired executive position with the USC. Must they take an unpaid leave of absence during the process?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, for at least two weeks.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, for the duration of the hiring process.

options.label: C
options.text: No — this is treated as an internal hiring process and no leave is required.

options.label: D
options.text: Only if they currently hold a Director role.

questionsConflict.explanation: Section 5.4 states paid employees applying for a hired executive position will not be required to take a leave of absence, as it is treated as an internal hiring process.

questionsConflict.question: A department wants to consult on filling a USC elected student leadership position and isn't sure who to go through. Per the policy, who should this consultation go through?

options.label: A
options.text: The Senior Manager, Information Systems.

options.label: B
options.text: The Human Resources Committee only.

options.label: C
options.text: The Board of Directors directly.

options.label: D
options.text: The President and Vice-Presidents.

questionsConflict.explanation: Section 5.6 states consultations for USC hired and elected student leadership positions shall go through the President and Vice-Presidents.

questionsDisc.question: An employee overhears a coworker repeatedly making unwelcome comments about another colleague's ethnic origin. What does this policy expect of the employee who overheard it?

options.label: A
options.text: To report it to their Manager/Supervisor and not willfully ignore a poisoned environment.

options.label: B
options.text: To wait and see if the targeted coworker files a complaint first.

options.label: C
options.text: To handle it informally themselves and not report it further.

options.label: D
options.text: Nothing, since they weren't the target of the comments.

questionsDisc.explanation: Sections 5.2.5 and 5.2.8 require Members not to willfully ignore a poisoned environment and to report incidents of discrimination or harassment to their Manager/Supervisor.

questionsDisc.question: A Member witnesses an immediate, escalating threat of violence in the workplace right now. What is the correct first step?

options.label: A
options.text: Document the incident and raise it at the next staff meeting.

options.label: B
options.text: Contact Campus Police at 911 (or ext. 83300) immediately, given the immediate danger.

options.label: C
options.text: Wait until the person involved calms down before reporting.

options.label: D
options.text: Email the Senior Manager, People and Development and wait for a reply.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 5.2.9 directs individuals to contact Campus Police at 911 or ext. 83300 in the event of an emergency or threat of violence.

questionsDisc.question: Does this policy apply to general student-to-student conduct within Western University?

options.label: A
options.text: Only if a USC Member is also directly involved.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, in all circumstances.

options.label: C
options.text: No — it is not intended to apply to general student-to-student or student-to-University contact.

options.label: D
options.text: Only during Orientation Week.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 1.3 states the Policy is not intended to be applied to general student-to-student or student-to-University contact within Western University.

questionsDisc.question: An anonymous but credible report suggests harassment may be occurring, though no formal complaint has been filed. What is the USC's obligation?

options.label: A
options.text: The matter can only be raised by the alleged victim.

options.label: B
options.text: The report must be dismissed as unverifiable.

options.label: C
options.text: No action is required without a formal, signed complaint.

options.label: D
options.text: The USC shall investigate reports or incidents of harassment, discrimination, or violence even without a formal complaint.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 4.3 states the USC shall investigate reports or incidents of harassment, discrimination, or violence even if no formal complaint has been made.

questionsDisc.question: Who administers this policy if the Senior Manager, People and Development is personally conflicted, such as being named in a complaint?

options.label: A
options.text: The Chief Operating Officer.

options.label: B
options.text: Any available Board member.

options.label: C
options.text: The chair of the Human Resources Committee.

options.label: D
options.text: The complainant's direct supervisor.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 3.1 states the Chief Operating Officer shall be responsible for administering the Policy if the Senior Manager, People and Development is involved in a complaint.

questionsDisc.question: Which of the following best matches the policy's definition of a 'poisoned environment'?

options.label: A
options.text: A single minor disagreement between coworkers.

options.label: B
options.text: A workplace where harassment or discrimination is so severe or frequent it creates an intimidating or hostile environment affecting work or academic performance.

options.label: C
options.text: Any workplace experiencing high stress or workload.

options.label: D
options.text: A workplace with inadequate physical facilities.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 2.4 defines a poisoned environment as one where harassment or discrimination is so severe or frequent that it creates an intimidating or hostile environment.

questionsDisc.question: A Member wants to know whether this policy's definition of harassment covers messages sent by text or instant message rather than in person. Is virtual conduct covered?

options.label: A
options.text: Only if the recipient forwards it to a supervisor within 24 hours.

options.label: B
options.text: No, only in-person conduct is covered.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes — the definition of harassment specifically includes virtual communication incidents.

options.label: D
options.text: Only if the message is sent during scheduled work hours.

questionsDisc.explanation: Section 2.2 states harassment includes virtual communication incidents.

questionsEarly.question: An employee's absence due to a work-related injury is expected to last only three days. Who is responsible for maintaining communication with them during this time?

options.label: A
options.text: The Senior Manager, People and Development, on a weekly basis.

options.label: B
options.text: The employee's supervisor.

options.label: C
options.text: The WSIB case manager directly.

options.label: D
options.text: The Joint Health and Safety Committee.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 4.1.9 states that where an absence is expected to be short-term (not exceeding five days), communication is maintained through the employee's supervisor.

questionsEarly.question: An employee's absence is now expected to exceed five days. Who takes over handling communications on behalf of the USC?

options.label: A
options.text: The employee's supervisor continues to handle it alone.

options.label: B
options.text: The Senior Manager, People and Development.

options.label: C
options.text: The Union.

options.label: D
options.text: WSIB directly.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 4.1.9 states that if an absence exceeds or is expected to exceed five days, the Senior Manager, People and Development shall handle communications on behalf of the USC.

questionsEarly.question: An investigation determines that an employee's injury claim was fraudulent. What is the consequence under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: A verbal warning only, regardless of severity.

options.label: B
options.text: Progressive discipline up to and including termination, and immediate reporting to WSIB.

options.label: C
options.text: No formal consequence unless it happens more than once.

options.label: D
options.text: The employee is simply removed from the return to work program with no further action.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 1.3 states a claim deemed fraudulent will result in progressive discipline up to and including termination, and will be reported to WSIB immediately.

questionsEarly.question: An employer wants to offer an employee 'suitable work' as part of a return to work plan. Which of the following is NOT one of the required characteristics of suitable work under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: It is available and can be started quickly.

options.label: B
options.text: It requires entirely new skills unrelated to the employee's existing abilities.

options.label: C
options.text: It is safe and within the employee's physical capabilities.

options.label: D
options.text: It restores pre-injury/illness earnings as much as reasonably possible.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 5.1.1 defines suitable work as available and quick to start, safe and within physical capabilities, using skills the employee has or can attain, and restoring earnings — not requiring entirely unrelated new skills.

questionsEarly.question: An employee sustains a work-related injury and is later declared fit to return to work in some capacity. At the latest, until what point must the USC continue making every effort to find suitable work?

options.label: A
options.text: Six months after the injury occurred.

options.label: B
options.text: The earlier of 12 months after being declared fit to return, or 24 months after the date of the injury/illness.

options.label: C
options.text: Indefinitely, with no time limit.

options.label: D
options.text: Only until the end of the calendar year in which the injury occurred.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 5.2.1 states the USC will make every effort to find suitable work up until the earlier of 12 months after being declared fit to return, or 24 months after the injury/illness date (among other listed end points).

questionsEarly.question: An employee disagrees with how the USC has handled their return to work plan and wants to raise a dispute. What is the first step under this policy?

options.label: A
options.text: File a complaint directly with WSIB.

options.label: B
options.text: Direct the dispute initially to the Chief Operating Officer.

options.label: C
options.text: Resign and reapply for the position.

options.label: D
options.text: Contact the Joint Health and Safety Committee directly.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 6.1 states disputes regarding the fulfillment of this policy may initially be directed to the Chief Operating Officer.

questionsEarly.question: A worker on modified duties is asked by the employer to attend an independent medical assessment. What is expected of the employee?

options.label: A
options.text: They may decline, since the request came from the employer rather than their own treating doctor.

options.label: B
options.text: They must comply with the recommendations of treating healthcare professionals and attend independent assessments as requested.

options.label: C
options.text: Only unionized employees are required to attend such assessments.

options.label: D
options.text: They may attend only if compensated separately for their time.

questionsEarly.explanation: Section 3.2.6 requires employees to comply with recommendations of treating healthcare professionals and attend independent assessments as requested.
